title: THE NATIVITY: THE BLOODLINE, BIRTHRIGHT, & THE MESSIAH

sense.text:
This is our true culture. “Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.” The law of life is our heritage, and our heritage is our culture.

When you read about the customs and laws the children of Israel kept, that is what God gave us: the new moon celebrations, the sabbath day, the feast of tabernacles. That is our heritage and our custom.

What our people in the Caribbean islands celebrate, what the West Indians in Brooklyn celebrate every Labor Day, even what black Americans follow here, is not our culture. Those so-called cultures were made up in slavery and after slavery, and most of it we learned from the white man. Black culture, West Indian culture: Negro, you got no culture. You were a slave. You were destroyed. All that stuff you follow, you made it up or you learned it from the white man.
“He made an everlasting covenant with them, and shewed them his judgments.” He showed us his judgments. The laws and the commandments, that is our heritage.

God showed Moses the future, and Moses saw our people in the very condition we are in today: on the streets of Babylon humping each other and acting the way we act. He saw it in the wilderness too, when they came down the mountain and the people rose up to play. Rising up to play is what you see in the street at carnival.

“And thou shalt become an astonishment”: people are shocked. The white people in Notting Hill stand at their windows and look down on us with disgust, astonished that black people hump each other in the street and call it a culture. Moses himself was astonished when he saw us in the future.

“A proverb, and a byword”: they call us out of our name. Watch at these niggas, they evil, they no good, they lascivious, they got no self-respect. That is how the nations watch us, “among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.” That is what is taking place in these festivities called carnival.

precepts.why:
“Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours”: we are hated, the nations look at us with hatred, because we are on the street dry humping each other and doing all kinds of filth openly.

“A scorn and a derision to them that are round about us.” They scorn us: I can't stand them, they in my community messing my street up with that carnival crap. “Thou makest us a byword among the heathen”: they call us out of our name and say all we do is act lewd like we got no sense.

“A shaking of the head among the people.” When the white people see us half naked on the street they shake their heads: look how they behaving. The nations watch us with scorn when they see us celebrate our so-called heritage. That is the byword Moses saw.

sense.text:
“Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”: when God planted us in the land and made us a nation, we were holy and right, in a right state of mind. We were not acting like what you see at carnival.

“How then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” What we have become is what you see on those streets: a degenerate vine, women humping each other and shaking it, and calling that black culture. That is not who we are. When God planted us as the children of Israel we did not act like that. We became degenerate, and the nations watch us with scorn.

precepts.why:
This is how the noble vine turned degenerate: we “were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.” We say carnival is our culture, but where in Africa do you see people doing exactly what these so-called West Indians do on Labor Day? You might see costumes, but not this. We learned it from the heathen, from the European colonizer.

So when the Europeans watch us with scorn and talk all that crap, it is their own culture we are practicing.

“And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them.” We served their idols, and it is a trap to us. That is why to this day we are out there acting the way we act.

sense.text:
“Envy thou not the oppressor”: in slavery the colonizers, Esau, held their masquerade balls, their orgies and parties right before Lent. The slaves were not allowed to take part, and we envied it.

“And choose none of his ways.” But we chose his ways. The French settlers brought their masquerade balls to Trinidad in the late 1700s; the slaves who could not join made their own version, added African drums and later the steel pan, and called it their culture. We learned carnival from the European, our slave master. It is not even an African culture. It is a European culture that goes back to Bacchus and into Lent, set up by the Roman Catholic Church.

God said don't envy the oppressor and choose none of his ways, and the slaves in the Caribbean did the very thing: envied those celebrations held in tribute to Bacchus, learned them, and called them their culture. You learned that in slavery.

“While I am yet alive with you this day, ye have been rebellious against the Lord; and how much more after my death?” Even in Moses' time we were evil, and he said we would be even worse when he was gone, because he saw it.

“Ye will utterly corrupt yourselves”: that is what we have done in these festivals and customs that were brought in to us. “And turn aside from the way which I have commanded you”: we turned aside from our own heritage and made our oppressor's heritage our heritage. That is what we are doing today.

“And evil will befall you in the latter days”: that is why we were brought over here in slavery. What Moses saw in that wilderness he saw us doing in the streets of New Orleans, of Brazil, of the Caribbean and of North America, “to provoke him to anger through the work of your hands.”

“For ye are yet carnal.” Carnal, carnival, carnivore: it all goes back to the same thing, the flesh. When Paul says you are carnal, he means being sinful, indulging the lust of the flesh.

Carnival comes from the Latin for raising the flesh: giving in to the flesh, overindulging your sexual desires. The Roman Catholic Church changed it to mean removing meat, farewell to the flesh, which is a false folk meaning. Carnival is the time of merrymaking before Lent. Lent begins on Ash Wednesday, forty days before Easter, when they abstain from meat and go to the priest with ashes on their foreheads to do penance for all they did in the days before.

So the pagans who came into the Church were allowed to keep their paganism: indulge, hold sex orgies, put on masquerade balls, and come on Wednesday for penance. Carnival is a Christian festival. Italy and Venice still keep it in the weeks before Lent, and Trinidad keeps it on the same days the Europeans keep it, which is why it began there. And Paul goes on, “for whereas there is among you envying”: that is the carnal man, the man of the flesh.
“Then were the days of unleavened bread.” Herod killed James and, seeing it pleased the Jews, took Peter also in the days of unleavened bread.

He kept Peter in prison “intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people.” Easter was a Roman pagan celebration, the goddess of fertility and spring, and it falls in the same season as the passover and the days of unleavened bread. Lent itself means springtime.

The Europeans took Easter and brought it into Christianity, the same way they brought the feast of Bacchus in through carnival. Carnival leads into Lent, and Lent leads up to Easter.

When “the fast of Bacchus was kept, the Jews were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.” Bacchus is the god of wine, and his feast is the bacchanal. The Greeks and Romans decorated themselves in ivy and flowers, crowns of leaves on their heads, and held orgies in his honor. That is what carnival is: the celebration of Bacchus. The same wreath is on the Christmas door.

In Trinidad we use the word bacchanal every day for drama, scandal and wild celebration, and we never knew why. A slave people learned that old Roman word from the Europeans celebrating carnival, because it was Bacchus they were celebrating. The carnival songs say it plainly: bring the bacchanal army, carnival is bacchanal. Carnival and bacchanal are the same thing.

So to all the carnival brothers and sisters on Labor Day saying it is part of your culture: it is European culture, Christian culture, Roman culture. They still celebrate it in Italy to this day.
Our forefathers were not all the most righteous men. Judah went down and lay with a Canaanite woman, the daughter of Shuah, which was forbidden for us.
He had three sons by her: Er, Onan and Shelah.

Judah gave Tamar to Er his firstborn, and Er was wicked and the Lord slew him. Then Judah told Onan to “raise up seed to thy brother.” Keep that in mind: raise up seed to thy brother. It plays a very important role in this lesson. When a brother dies leaving no children, his brother raises up seed for him.

“Onan knew that the seed should not be his”, so he pulled out and “spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.” That verse alone destroys any doubt about what seed is: seed is sperm. The inheritance would not be his, so he would not give seed, and the Lord slew him also.

With her husband dead and no child, Tamar went back to her father's house, because before marriage her father was her head. Judah told her to wait till Shelah was grown; he was too young. There was no older woman taking up a little boy for a husband.

Judah broke his word and never gave her Shelah, so she put off her widow's garments, covered her face, and sat by the way. Judah took her for an harlot and lay with her, leaving his signet, bracelets and staff as a pledge, “and she conceived by him.”

About three months later she began to show, living in her father's house with her husband dead: she played the harlot. “Bring her forth, and let her be burnt”: set that hoe on fire. That was the law for a whore: you play the whore, you get burned alive. But she sent the pledge: “By the man, whose these are, am I with child.” Judah acknowledged them: “She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.” He knew her again no more, because it was wrong in the first place.

She bare twins. One put out his hand and the midwife bound a scarlet thread on it, then he drew it back and his brother came out first: Pharez, meaning a breach. Then came Zarah with the scarlet thread. Pharez is the line that leads to Boaz and David.

precepts.why:
Moses later sets down the law our forefathers already knew by tradition from Adam: when brethren dwell together and one dies with no child, “her husband's brother shall go in unto her,” and “the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.”

To succeed in the name of the dead does not mean the child takes the dead man's name. It means the child inherits the dead man's possession, his land, so that it stays in his name and is not lost. The brother raises up a surrogate seed in honor of his dead brother.

The man who refuses does what Onan did. The widow goes to the elders, looses his shoe and spits in his face: “So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house.” And he carries the shameful title forever: “The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.” He broke love your neighbour as yourself. That is why the history of Ruth is so important.

sense.text: Er, Onan and Shelah were born to Judah of the Canaanitess; Er was evil and the Lord slew him. Tamar bare Pharez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah were five.
The sons of Pharez: Hezron, the oldest. Keep that name in mind.
The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara. These became famous and very wise men, and many men were named after them.
Achar, “the troubler of Israel”, is Achan, the one who took the Babylonish garment in Joshua's time and caused problems for Israel.

Hezron had Jerahmeel, Ram and Chelubai, which is Caleb (a different Caleb). Ram begat Amminadab, and Amminadab begat Nahshon, “prince of the children of Judah.” A prince family, a royal family of Judah.

Nahshon begat Salma, Salma begat Boaz, Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse, the father of David. These men were not ordinary men: Nahshon was a prince and a captain, they were warriors, and Boaz came from that line, the line of Pharez, the one who broke forth.

precepts.why: Solomon “was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda.” Those are the same sons of Zerah of Judah. They were very wise, and Solomon surpassed even them in wisdom.
“Of Judah; Nahshon the son of Amminadab.” The same Nahshon, named over Judah when Israel was numbered.
“Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.” These men had serious status: princes and captains, leaders of Judah.

“Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife.” Aaron, Moses' brother, married into the tribe of Judah, into this princely house. She bare him Nadab and Abihu, who burned strange fire and were killed, and Eleazar and Ithamar. Eleazar became the high priest in Joshua's time, and his mother was Judah.

So the families of the priests and the kings married together. No coincidence: that is how John the Baptist and Christ come to be cousins.

sense.text: “In the days when the judges ruled” there was a famine, as in Jacob's time, and Elimelech of Beth-lehem-judah went with Naomi and their two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, to sojourn in Moab to survive. They were Ephrathites of Bethlehem: they had land in Bethlehem, Judah.

Elimelech died, his sons took wives of Moab, Orpah and Ruth, and “they dwelled there about ten years.” You do not live under a bridge for ten years. They bought land in Moab too. So this family owned land in two places, Moab and Bethlehem, and that plays a role later. Then Mahlon and Chilion died, and Naomi lost all her men.

The famine was over, so Naomi turned home to Judah, to her husband's land, and told her daughters-in-law to go back to their mothers' houses. They said, “Surely we will return with thee unto thy people”: thy people. They are not our women, not our sisters. Naomi said she had no more sons in her womb to give them; you are Moab, I am Israel, go home.

Orpah went “back unto her people, and unto her gods.” This is not an Israelite woman: she went back to her own people and her own gods. There are doctrines teaching that Ruth was an Israelite. She was not. She was a heathen. What Boaz did, taking a heathen, was not right, but it happened.

Ruth clave: “thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.” A heathen saying, I will go with you as if I am an Israelite and serve your God. It is no promise to her; she is simply cleaving to an Israelite woman, the same way the nations will cleave in the kingdom.

They came to Bethlehem. “Call me not Naomi, call me Mara”: Naomi means pleasant and Mara means bitter. I went out full with a husband and two sons, and came home empty. And Ruth is named plainly: “Ruth the Moabitess.”

precepts.why: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.” Ruth begins “in the days when the judges ruled”: the time when there was no king and Israel did what they wanted, including taking heathen women.

“Ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.” That is Ruth: we will go with you, because your God is the real God. The nations will cleave to Israel in the kingdom the same way she clave to Naomi.

sense.text: This is a trial about the land. Elimelech had land, and he and both his sons died. Who does it go to? It must be taken up by the next of kin, the same law Onan broke. Boaz took ten elders of the city to sit in council on the inheritance.

Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech's.” Boaz could not just take it; there was a kinsman closer in line. “For there is none to redeem it beside thee; and I am after thee.” Boaz was last in line, so he offered it first to the nearer kinsman, who said, I will redeem it.

But “thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.” If you want the land, you take the woman and raise up seed to the man that land belongs to. The land does not become yours; it belongs to the seed you raise up. That is why the Lord moved Ruth to stay with Naomi: to keep that name and that land alive.

“I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance.” He passed his right to Boaz. Plucking off the shoe goes back to the law of the man who refuses his brother's wife. Here it is no shame: he is giving his right over to another, and the shoe is the testimony.

Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and Ruth the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” He raised up a child in Mahlon's name, so the land stays in that family. It does not belong to Boaz; it belongs to Mahlon's line. Because he loved his neighbour as himself, he did it. That is what love your neighbour as yourself means.

Land is very important. If you have it, keep it and give it to your children. Do not sell it off. Judah had millions of acres here in America, and Esau stole it through laws like eminent domain and by buying out some distant kin for a little money.

The elders blessed Boaz: “like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Israel,” and “let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Judah.” Pharez is his great-great-grandfather. Ruth gets a shout out because, if she had not stayed, that land would have been lost to the family.

“When he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception.” That is what happens when a man goes in unto a woman: conception. Keep that word in mind; it is very important today. If “the Lord gave her conception” meant what the Christians say it means at Christ's birth, then God had sex with Ruth. That is how ridiculous that doctrine is.

The women said, “There is a son born to Naomi.” Boaz raised up seed in the name of Naomi's dead husband, so it is as if the child is her own. They called him Obed, “the father of Jesse, the father of David”, coming out of the princely line of Nahshon.

The generations of Pharez again: Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon, “Boaz begat Obed.” It does not say Mahlon begat Obed. Mahlon was dead. Raising up seed to your dead brother (levirate marriage) does not make the dead man the father. The doctrine that Obed had two dads is wacky. The land falls under the dead man's name for inheritance; the lineage goes through Boaz, his real father. They are the same tribe anyway. You do not inherit a tribe; you inherit the land.

precepts.why: “Naomi had a kinsman of her husband's, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech; and his name was Boaz.” This is Nahshon's grandson Boaz, the son of Salmon, a mighty man with wealth: the kinsman who sits down at the gate.

Christ came to “Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: it is all the same thing, the inheritance. Jacob bought Joseph that land.

Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, “and he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem's father, for an hundred pieces of money.” He bought it from a Hamite, and erected an altar there. This explains the history in John 4.

Israel told Joseph, “I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” They bought the land first, and then Simeon and Levi went crazy and killed them all.

They buried the bones of Joseph “in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor”, “and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground is the land of inheritance given to Ephraim. So when Naomi sells a parcel of land, it is the inheritance.

“I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” It means what it says. In the beginning God allotted every family its land and inheritance, and those families are here today. Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance given to their family back then.

And it says every man. Sisters divorce us and take half our stuff, but by God the inheritance belongs to the men. The wives benefit because they are married to us, like the earth belonged to Adam and Eve benefited as his helper.
“The children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Every family that came out of Egypt was allotted land and inheritance, and it will be given back to them.

sense.text: Nahshon begat Salma, Salma begat Boaz, Boaz Obed, Obed Jesse, and Jesse's sons are numbered: David was “the seventh.”
David's sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah's sons were Abishai, Joab and Asahel, so Joab was David's cousin.
“The father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmeelite.” That is a copyist's error. He was an Israelite. There are no Ishmeelites in this line.

precepts.why: Amasa “was a man's son, whose name was Ithra an Israelite.” Ithra or Jether is the same man, and he was an Israelite. So the word Ishmeelite in Chronicles was copied wrong, and nobody should be confused into thinking Ishmael is in David's family line.

sense.text: The sons of Caleb and of Hezron. Jair “had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead”, and with Kenath and its towns, “even threescore cities.” When we say land we will inherit, don't think of an acre. We owned cities: somebody literally owned the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, with castles on them, winter houses and summer houses.
The sons of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn, down to Sheshan. Keep the name Sheshan in mind.

“Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha.” An Egyptian servant tells you where Israel was at this time: in Egypt, in captivity, with no land of inheritance.

Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant, and the line goes down from Attai to Elishama. People read this and say an Egyptian married into the tribe and became Judah. No. This was when we were in Egypt.

When Israel came out of Egypt and inherited the land, this line got no land, because the land passes by the paternal bloodline and this line goes back to an Egyptian servant. They lived among us, but they inherited no land. That is why it is recorded here: not to bring Hamites into the lineage, but to keep the land in the paternal line. All of Jerahmeel's other sons had sons, and they got the land. It is the same reason that after Persia, if you could not show your genealogy, who your father was, you were given no inheritance and a Levite could not serve.

precepts.why:
This is what Israelites did when they had no son. Abram said, “what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?” “Lo, one born in my house is mine heir.” He was going to give his land to his eldest servant, a Syrian.

The Lord said, “This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.” Heir goes with inheritance and heirloom: what is passed down the line. Not to a heathen over here, but to your own. So Sheshan, with no son, gave his inheritance to his Egyptian servant in Egypt.

When we were in the land, a man with no sons and only daughters was a rarity. The daughters of Zelophehad said their father “died in his own sin, and had no sons. Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son?” Now you know what law Boaz was fulfilling.

The case was so different that Moses went to the Lord, and the Lord said, “The daughters of Zelophehad speak right.” Let them keep their father's land. And it became law: no son, it passes to his daughter; no daughter, to his brethren; then to his father's brethren, his male cousins; then “unto his kinsman that is next to him of his family.” It is a paternal line. That is Boaz: next in line.

Then the fathers of Gilead worried: if Zelophehad's daughters marry into another tribe, Benjamin or Ephraim or Levi, the husband inherits the land and it is taken from our lot, and even in the jubile it is put to the tribe they married into.

The Lord said they speak well: “Let them marry to whom they think best; only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.” So “every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance” marries within her father's tribe, and the land does not move from tribe to tribe. The land of Israel is a paternal inheritance.

There is no sin in marrying a woman of another tribe: Aaron married into Judah, because Amminadab had sons as well as daughters. The command only applies when a man has daughters and no sons, to keep the land. And now that we are all in captivity with no land, the word is: marry within your own nation.

sense.text: Tobit, of the tribe of Nephthali, was led captive by the king of Assyria out of Thisbe in Galilee.

When he was young, all the tribe of Nephthali and his father's house fell into idolatry and “sacrificed unto the heifer Baal.” “But I alone went often to Jerusalem at the feasts”, giving his tenths to the sons of Aaron. He was left an orphan by his father, who went into idolatry and abandoned him, and was raised by his grandmother. Some of the men became wicked and abandoned their children.
“I married Anna of mine own kindred, and of her I begat Tobias.”

In captivity in Nineve his brethren ate “of the bread of the Gentiles”, things offered to idols. “But I kept myself from eating; Because I remembered God with all my heart.” And the most High gave him favour, so that he became the king's purveyor, over the king's accounts.

While he was well off he looked out for his brethren, fed the hungry, clothed the naked, and buried any of his nation he found cast about the walls of Nineve. When Sennacherib came back from Judea, where an angel had killed his men, he took it out on Israel and killed many in his wrath, and Tobit buried them “privily”, secretly, though he worked for that king.

He was ratted out, became a fugitive, and “all my goods were forcibly taken away”, even his wife and son. That is an example of what is coming: when you go against this system and teach against it and refuse to support the beast, everything you have will be taken from you.

Within fifty-five days the king's two sons killed him, and Sarchedonus reigned, and set over all his accounts “Achiacharus my brother Anael's son.” His nephew had status next unto the king, and he interceded for Tobit, and Tobit returned to Nineve. Tobit was not alone in being righteous in captivity: his nephew looked out for him the way he had looked out for his own people, and the Lord looked out for him.

His wife and son were restored to him, most likely having been imprisoned as enemies of the state; that is the consequence of serving God, and the time is coming when you will have to choose. And it was “in the feast of Pentecost”: Tobit was in captivity, not in Jerusalem, and he kept the holy day. You heretics who say you cannot keep the feasts in captivity, what was Tobit doing?
He sent his son to bring a poor man of their brethren “who is mindful of the Lord.” He was not the only one serving the Lord in captivity.

One of their nation was strangled in the marketplace, and before tasting his meat Tobit took him up and buried him after sunset, and his neighbours mocked him: he did this before and fled, and he still has not learned.

Sleeping by the wall, sparrows muted warm dung into his eyes and he went blind. Anna took women's work to support them, and when she brought home a kid he accused her of stealing it, and she threw it back at him: “Where are thine alms and thy righteous deeds?”
Tobit asked God to take his life: “it is profitable for me to die rather than to live.”

The same day in Ecbatane, Sara the daughter of Raguel had “been married to seven husbands, whom Asmodeus the evil spirit had killed, before they had lain with her.” They were her husbands before they lay with her, because she was promised to them: the espousal is the marriage. Her father's maids mocked her and she grew so sorrowful she thought to strangle herself. “I am the only daughter of my father”: Raguel had no son, only one daughter.

“Neither hath he any child to be his heir, neither any near kinsman, nor any son of his alive, to whom I may keep myself for a wife.” Remember the importance of inheritance: she has nobody to marry who can keep her father's land.
The prayers of both were heard, and Raphael was sent to heal Tobit's eyes and “to give Sara the daughter of Raguel for a wife to Tobias”, “because she belonged to Tobias by right of inheritance.”

Tobit tells his son, “take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife.” Marry within your own, not a heathen woman. “We are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”: Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob all married within their own kindred, “and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.”
“Despise not in thy heart thy brethren, the sons and daughters of thy people, in not taking a wife of them.” “For lewdness is the mother of famine.”
Raguel is Tobias' cousin and “hath one only daughter, named Sara.” “For to thee doth the right of her appertain, seeing thou only art of her kindred.” She is the only heir left of Raguel.

“Raguel cannot marry her to another according to the law of Moses, but he shall be guilty of death, because the right of inheritance doth rather appertain to thee than to any other.” Giving your land to someone it does not belong to is worthy of death. Land is a heavy thing; you cannot give it away to anybody.

The seven men “all died in the marriage chamber”, when they came together, before they could consummate. Tobias was afraid: “I am the only son of my father.” He is the only son of his father and she is the only daughter of hers.

The angel reminded him of “the precepts which thy father gave thee, that thou shouldest marry a wife of thine own kindred,” and called him “O my brother.” “She is appointed unto thee from the beginning.” She was meant to be his from the beginning.
Raguel saw how like the young man was to Tobit his cousin, and when he learned he was Tobit's son he wept and blessed him: “Thou art the son of an honest and good man.”

Raguel said it was right for him to marry his daughter, but told him the truth about the seven men; Tobias would eat nothing till they swore together. “Take her from henceforth according to the manner, for thou art her cousin.”
He gave her “after the law of Moses”, and wrote “an instrument of covenants, and sealed it”: the marriage certificate.
“Prepare another chamber, and bring her in thither”: the wedding chamber.
“After that they were both shut in together”: being shut in together, coming together, is the wedding feast and the marriage chamber. Keep that in mind.
Tobias prayed, “I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly.” They came together and consummated; now she is his wife.

Tobias did not die, so Raguel had the grave filled, kept the wedding feast fourteen days, and swore that Tobias should “take the half of his goods” now, “and should have the rest when I and my wife be dead.” Raguel passed his inheritance to his son-in-law of the same tribe.
Raguel “gave him Sara his wife, and half his goods, servants, and cattle, and money.”
“Honour thy father and thy mother in law, which are now thy parents.”
Tobit received his sight and went out to meet his daughter-in-law at the gate of Nineve, blessing her and her father and mother.
His brother's son came, “and Tobias' wedding was kept seven days with great joy.”
Tobit foretold that Nineve would be overthrown, “and Jerusalem shall be desolate, and the house of God in it shall be burned”: by Babylon.

When Tobit and Anna died, Tobias went to Ecbatane to his father-in-law, buried him and his wife, “and he inherited their substance, and his father Tobit's.” He received half when he left, and the rest when they died. He inherited both lands, his own father's and his parents-in-law's, because they were of the same tribe and Raguel had no son. Keep that in mind.
“The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.” Generation goes back to genealogy, genes, genetics, Genesis.
Pharez and Zarah of Thamar, the twins; Aminadab begat Naasson, the brother of Elisheba whom Aaron married; Salmon begat Booz, and Booz begat Obed of Ruth.
David begat Solomon “of her that had been the wife of Urias”, Bathsheba.
From Solomon the kings go down: Roboam, Abia, Asa, through Ezekias (Hezekiah), Manasses, Amon and Josias.
“And Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren, about the time they were carried away to Babylon.” Jechonias was Josiah's grandson, not his son. Hold that.

precepts.why:
Jehoiakim served Nebuchadnezzar three years and rebelled, and the Lord sent bands against Judah for the sins of Manasseh and the innocent blood he shed. Jehoiakim is the father of Jechonias. “Jehoiachin his son reigned in his stead.” Jehoiachin is Jechonias.

He reigned three months, did evil like his father, and went out to the king of Babylon, who took him, his mother, his wives, his officers and the mighty of the land captive to Babylon, and left only the poorest. Then the king “made Mattaniah his father's brother king in his stead, and changed his name to Zedekiah.” His uncle took the throne.

Zedekiah rebelled too. When the city was broken up he tried to flee and was overtaken in the plains of Jericho. “They slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.” His heirs were gone. Zedekiah was the last king of Judah. So who is left?

“In the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin”, Evil-merodach lifted up his head out of prison, “set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon”, and gave him “a continual allowance”, a daily rate all his life. Jechonias was locked up thirty-six or thirty-seven years, then got mercy and status in captivity in Babylon.

The sons of Josiah: Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah (Mattaniah), and Shallum. The sons of Jehoiakim: “Jeconiah his son.” Jehoiachin, Jeconiah, Coniah and Jechonias are the same man.

“The sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son.” Whether Assir is a son or a title meaning the captive does not matter: Salathiel is the son of Jeconiah, born while his father was a captive with status in Babylon. Salathiel's brothers were Malchiram, Pedaiah and the rest, “and the sons of Pedaiah were, Zerubbabel, and Shimei.”

“Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel” stood up with Jeshua the priest and built the altar. Shealtiel is Salathiel, the same man in 1 Chronicles 3:17, Matthew 1:12 and Luke 3:27. This Zerubbabel, the son of Salathiel, was responsible for building the second temple.

But Salathiel had a brother, Pedaiah, and Pedaiah also had a son named Zerubbabel. Is that a problem? No. Zerubbabel means born in Babylon. When Jeconiah got status in Babylon and had children there, his sons named their children for where they were born, so Zerubbabel was not the only Zerubbabel: it was a common name. That is important, and we come back to it.

sense.text: The Lord speaking to David: “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.” Out of the bowels: sperm. And when David died, whose kingdom did it become? Solomon's kingdom.

“He shall build an house for my name.” Solomon built the first house; Babylon burned it, as Tobit said; Zerubbabel built the second. “And I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.” It is twofold.
“I will be his father, and he shall be my son.” “Thy throne shall be established for ever.” When David died it was not Nathan's kingdom or any other son's kingdom. It was Solomon's.

precepts.why:
Solomon was “young and tender”, and the house had to be “exceeding magnifical”: an old word for magnificent, grand and glorious. David prepared abundantly and charged Solomon to build it.

David could not build it: “Thou hast shed blood abundantly, and hast made great wars.” The Lord used David like a lawnmower; he slew everybody until they all paid tribute and were afraid of him, so Solomon could build in peace. There is no peace without bloodshed.

“A son shall be born to thee, who shall be a man of rest”, “for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness unto Israel in his days.” Solomon comes from shalom, peace, the same as Jerusalem. “He shall build an house for my name; and he shall be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.” Twofold again.

God chose Judah, the house of Jesse, and David, “And of all my sons, (for the Lord hath given me many sons,) he hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.” “Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever.” It does not say Solomon and his brethren's kingdom. It says his kingdom.

And David “gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch”: the blueprints of the temple, every chamber, the place of the mercy seat, the courses of the priests, the gold by weight. Solomon fulfilled his father's design, and it came “by the spirit”: “the Lord made me understand in writing by his hand upon me.” The Lord moved David's hand to draw it out.

sense.text: Concerning Jehoiakim: “He shall be buried with the burial of an ass.”

“Though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon my right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence”: into Babylon, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. Jehoiachin, Jeconiah, Jechonias and Coniah are one person with four names. He and his mother would be cast into another country, and there die.
“But to the land whereunto they desire to return, thither shall they not return.” He would never return to rule over Judah again. He would stay captive in Babylon till death.
“Wherefore are they cast out, he and his seed, and are cast into a land which they know not?” His seed is his children. They would be born in captivity, not on the throne.

“Write ye this man childless.” Was he childless? No: verse 28 speaks of his seed, and Salathiel was his son, born in Babylon. He is written childless because “no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah”, since they would be in captivity.

The line was not cursed. They were put in captivity like everybody else. There is no scripture that says Coniah's line is cursed and can never be kings; that doctrine was made up to justify a virgin birth, like Christmas and carnival and Lent and Easter. When Christ came on the scene nobody of Judah sat on the throne: Rome ruled and put an Edomite, Herod, there.

And whose kingdom is it? Solomon's. Rehoboam his son reigned after him, then his son. No one outside Solomon's loins can sit on that throne. So if Christ is not of Solomon's line, he is not entitled to it.
“I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” That is Christ.

“Behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua.” The stone and the branch are the same. The argument is that Joseph cannot be Christ's father because of a virgin birth, and that his right to the throne came through his mother in Luke 3. Matthew 1 is Solomon's lineage, and that is Joseph's line.

precepts.why:
“Who art thou, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel thou shalt become a plain”: Babylon brought down. “And he shall bring forth the headstone thereof with shoutings, crying, Grace, grace unto it.” Zerubbabel brings forth the headstone, and in chapter 3 the Lord brings forth the Branch, the stone. Who is the headstone? Christ. So how will Zerubbabel bring him forth? Through his line. And Zerubbabel comes out of Solomon's line, not Nathan's.

It is twofold: Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple, a literal stone, and through his loins he brought forth the other stone, Christ, who brings us grace, grace.
“The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” The stone laid before Joshua is the headstone Zerubbabel brings forth: Christ.

“Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord.” Zerubbabel laid the foundation of the second temple, and out of him came the foundation, Christ, who builds the holy temple, which is us: “ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.”

sense.text: “About the time they were carried away to Babylon.” They cannot sit on the throne in captivity.
“After they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel.” When Jeconiah got status and wages in Babylon, he begat sons there. Zerubbabel never sat on the throne.

From Zorobabel down to Matthan, “And Matthan begat Jacob; And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” Joseph's father was Jacob, and Joseph descends from Zerubbabel: a line of kings, out of the kingdom of Solomon. Joseph should have been heir to the throne, but in captivity he could not be. Rome called the shots and put an Edomite on the throne, and it will not be taken back until Christ returns and conquers Edom.

“Being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph”: everyone understood that. “Which was the son of Heli.” But Matthew says Joseph's father was Jacob. So who is Heli, and why is Joseph written here? You understand it if you remember inheritance: a man with daughters and no sons.

Tobit's son married Raguel's only daughter, and when Raguel died his land went to his son-in-law, so in Raguel's record of inheritance he is written as his son. That is why Joseph is here: Heli had no sons, and left his inheritance to Joseph, his son-in-law. Heli is Mary's father. Joseph inherited Heli's land as his son, the way the son-in-law inherits when the father-in-law has no sons. That is why we went over inheritance the whole time.

“Which was the son of Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel, which was the son of Neri.” This is not the Zerubbabel and Salathiel of Matthew: Matthew's Salathiel was the son of Jechonias, not Neri. Zerubbabel was a common name for a son born in Babylon. Mary's line had its own.

“Which was the son of Nathan, which was the son of David.” This is Nathan's line. Can you have two great-grandfathers on your father's side? No. Joseph cannot descend from both Nathan and Solomon. So this is a different lineage, Mary's, both of the same tribe, and that is why Joseph could inherit both lands.

And Christ cannot take his right to the throne through Mary's line, because Nathan's side does not sit on the throne. Even Nebuchadnezzar, a heathen, put Zedekiah of Solomon's line on the throne, not Nathan's sons. Nowhere in the Bible do Nathan's children sit on the throne. The kingdom belongs to Solomon.

precepts.why:
“There stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas.” Christ had an aunt: Mary had a sister, but we read of no brother.

“Woman, behold thy son!” “Behold thy mother!” “And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.” Joseph was already dead and gone; she was a widow with no brother to go to, so John took her in. He never called her mother, because he knew the Christians would call her mother of God. He called her what Adam called his wife: woman. (Don't you call your mother woman; you are not Christ.)

“Is not this the carpenter's son? is not his mother called Mary? and his brethren, James, and Joses, and Simon, and Judas?” James wrote the book of James and Judas wrote Jude. Christ had brothers, “And his sisters, are they not all with us?” More than one sister. So much for Mary never knowing a man.

Mattathias had five sons: Joannan, Simon, Judas, Eleazar, “and Jonathan.” Joannan and Jonathan are the same name, John and John. Israel commonly named children the same name, like George Foreman's sons. So Mary and her sister both being Mary is no problem.
“Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.”

“Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.” His own neighbours knew his family and his background: we grew up with him, he is from the hood like us, what is he talking about, son of God?

sense.text: “Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?” Son of man, not son of woman, not son of the Holy Spirit. Son of man.

precepts.why: “And he said unto me, Son of man, stand upon thy feet.” Ezekiel is called son of man.
“Understand, O son of man.” Daniel is called son of man. Ezekiel and Daniel both had parents, and Christ is called son of man the same way. There is nothing to be confused about.

sense.text: Luke wrote “that thou mightest know the certainty of those things.” Luke knew things of certainty. Some say Luke was not one of the twelve so his genealogy in Luke 3 is bugged out; all of Acts is proven historically accurate. And if you doubt Luke, where else will you find John the Baptist's lineage? Only Luke tells us John was a Levite.

Zacharias and Elisabeth were both of Aaron, “walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless”: in the New Testament righteousness is keeping the commandments. They had no child; she was barren and both “well stricken in years.”
“Thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.” Future tense. The angel named John before he was conceived.

“He shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother's womb.” Filled with the Holy Ghost in his mother's womb. Keep that in mind: the same holiness is said of Christ, and John was conceived when his father went home to his wife.

“Whereby shall I know this? for I am an old man”: when will this happen? Gabriel answered that he would be dumb “until the day that these things shall be performed.” The performance is his wife getting pregnant in her old age.

“He departed to his own house. And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived.” It does not say he went in unto her. It says he went home and she conceived, and nobody questions how. We all know what happened. But when Mary goes home and is with child, it is a virgin birth. It is the same exact thing.

She “hid herself five months”, because an old woman walking around with a belly looks crazy, and her reproach was being called barren. That is a miracle in itself: conceiving at an old age, like Sarah.

In the sixth month Gabriel was sent to Nazareth, “To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David”: of Solomon's line. “The angel came in unto her”: he came in and talked with her. Nothing else.

“Thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.” The same words said to Zacharias: thou shalt call his name John. To conceive you need sperm; the swimmers must reach the egg.
“The Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David.” That is Solomon's kingdom, which only Solomon's seed can sit on.
“How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?” The same question Zacharias asked: when will this happen? She was espoused to Joseph but had not yet come together with him. This was before the meeting.

“That holy thing which shall be born of thee”: the same holiness said of John, filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother's womb. Their lives run parallel. And “shall be called the Son of God” is future tense.

“Thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived”: also. The same way she conceived, you will conceive. That is reading comprehension. “For with God nothing shall be impossible”: the same way Elisabeth gave birth in old age. It is not talking about a virgin birth. Mary asked how, and the Lord answered, I will guide you; nothing is impossible with God.
“Be it unto me according to thy word”: if you say so, so be it. The angel left, and she was not pregnant yet. She went to the hill country of Juda to visit Elisabeth and Zacharias, her cousins.
The babe leaped in Elisabeth's womb. “There shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord.” Shall: she was not pregnant yet. The performance would come when she went home.
“Mary abode with her about three months, and returned to her own house.” Elisabeth was six months along, so Mary stayed till she gave birth, then went home, to Nazareth, where Joseph was.

They would have named him Zacharias after his father, but his mother said, “he shall be called John.” “There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name”: they always used the same family names. Zacharias wrote, “His name is John.”
“What manner of child shall this be!” Born of an old couple, he would be special.

Zacharias answers: “And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest”, and Christ “shall be called the Son of the Highest.” It is parallel; the same is said of both. John goes before the face of the Lord, rolling out the red carpet, teaching them Christ before he came and baptizing them for the remission of sins.
“And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit.” The same is said of Christ.

precepts.why: “When he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.” That is how conception works: the Lord gives conception when a man goes in unto his wife. Thou shalt conceive means the same thing. The first time Joseph touched her she got pregnant, the Lord made it so.

“If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child”: a woman conceives seed through intercourse. It is the same seed Onan spilled on the ground knowing the inheritance would not be his. Everything said to Mary was fulfilled the same way it was fulfilled when Zacharias went home.

“The whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew”: the whole creature is Israel, the whole nation coming out of Egypt, made new, serving the commandments.

“As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp”, then the dry land and the way out of the Red sea, “Wherethrough all the people went that were defended with thy hand.” What did the cloud overshadowing us do? It defended us and led us through the Red sea. That is what overshadow means.

God casts down the hills and fills the valleys “that Israel may go safely”, and “every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God. For God shall lead Israel with joy.” To overshadow is to lead, guide and defend.

So “the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee” does not mean impregnating her. It means the Lord would guide her to where she had to go, to the man she was espoused to, the same way he led Zacharias home to his wife.

“Man's goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?” The Lord guides us and overshadows us every day, like when something tells you to stop and pick something up and a car flies by that would have killed you.

Mary did not understand her way either: how shall this be, seeing I know not a man? The Lord said, don't worry, you will fulfil the scriptures, I will guide you. He had plans for Mary, the same way he guides all of us.

“And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom.” The very words said of John. Their lives are parallel. So the same way Elisabeth conceived with Zacharias, Mary conceived with Joseph. It is that clear.

sense.text: Cesar Augustus decreed the world should be taxed, “every one into his own city.” This is factual history.

“Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth.” Mary returned home to Nazareth, and that is where Joseph was: the same way Zacharias went home to Elisabeth, Mary went home and ran into Joseph. They left Nazareth together for Bethlehem, “because he was of the house and lineage of David.”

“To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife.” Roman censuses were tied to taxation and to property: people registered where they lived or where they held taxable property. Joseph went to Bethlehem because he had land there. He had his own family's land and Mary's father's land, just like Tobias. And Mary was “great with child”, ready to deliver.

“The days were accomplished that she should be delivered”: nine months, a full term.

They say Christ could not have been born the regular way because he would be conceived in sin. But Mary was born in sin too. If he grew nine months in her womb, fed by her, he was in a sinful womb. So they invented the immaculate conception: Mary had no sin. Then Mary is a savior too, as perfect as Christ: two saviors. You have no choice but to deify Mary in that doctrine. It is religious feminism.
“Her firstborn son”: Jesus is the oldest, and she had more children after. There was no room in the inn because it was crowded: passover season, with everyone being taxed.
“Shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.” You do not keep your flock out at night in the winter. It was a warm season. That kills December.
“This shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe.” Who is the sign, the mother or the baby? The baby. It is always the child that is the sign, not the woman.

“His name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.” The angel named him before Mary lay with Joseph, the same way he named John before Zacharias went in to his wife.

“Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him.” If he was born miraculously, what is there to marvel at? They marvelled because he was born the regular way, and these great things were being said about their son.
“This child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel; and for a sign”: again the child is the sign, not Mary.
“They returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.” Luke abbreviates; Matthew 2 fills in the years between.

precepts.why: “The angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth.” That is where Mary lived, and Joseph went up “out of the city of Nazareth.” They were both in Nazareth.
“I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth.” There was no room in the inn, so his mother brought him forth under an apple tree.

sense.text: The wise men asked, “Where is he that is born King of the Jews?” The scribes answered from the prophet Micah: in Bethlehem.

Herod asked what time the star appeared: how long it had been out there since Christ was born. “Go and search diligently for the young child.” A young child, a toddler, not a newborn. This was years later, not his birthday. And Herod said he would come “and worship him also”, not celebrate his birthday.
“When they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother.” A house in Bethlehem: that was Joseph's house.
The angel told Joseph to flee into Egypt, further into Africa, and they stayed there till Herod died: they had a place to stay there too.
Herod slew the children “in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under”, by the time the star had been out. Rachel weeping for her children: he was killing Benjamin too.

When Herod was dead Joseph came back, but Archelaus reigned in Judea, so he turned aside into Galilee and dwelt in Nazareth. So Joseph had a place in Bethlehem and a place in Nazareth, three with Egypt. That is why he went to Bethlehem to be taxed: he had property there.
“They declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers.” By the house of their fathers, not their mothers.

precepts.why: Those who came up from Babylon “could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they were of Israel.” Your father's house determines your race and your nation. That is why Christ's lineage goes through Joseph.

sense.text: “Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same.” The children are the disciples, us. Christ took part of the same flesh and blood.
“He took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham”: flesh and blood.
“Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.” In all things, not some things. How is that possible except with a father and a mother?

precepts.why: “It is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda.” He sprang out of Judah by his father.

sense.text:
“When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child.” Coming together is the customary wedding feast, as with Tobias and Sara shut in together. Before the wedding feast, they lay together. They were already espoused, so there was no fornication. Betrothal is marriage: if a woman is betrothed and another man lies with her, it is adultery. Once her father promised her, she could marry no one else.

“Of the Holy Ghost” means a child of prophecy: the child the Holy Ghost had spoken of through the prophets.

Joseph, “being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.” The commentators say he wanted to divorce her secretly because the child was not his. But if he was a just man and his espoused wife was pregnant by another, the just thing was death, not hiding her. And if he was divorcing her secretly, he was hiding sin; how is that just?

A public example means being put to death in public, stoned for being a whore. She would have gone back to her father's house showing, like Tamar three months in, and been killed for what they did together. So Joseph owned up: he thought about hiding her, because the baby was his. Why would anyone hide a pregnant woman he did not get pregnant? There is no way around that question.

“Fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost”: she was already his wife because she was espoused to him. What is conceived in her is of the prophecy of 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132.
“Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.”
“That it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet”: Matthew is pointing back to Isaiah 7, a child born as a sign that God was with them.

precepts.why: Jacob served seven years for Rachel and said, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.” “And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.” That evening “he went in unto her.” Coming together is the wedding feast. Joseph and Mary lay together before that feast.

Elisabeth “conceived, and hid herself five months.” Putting her away privily is the same thing: to hide her. Joseph was minded to hide her privately, because he knew he had lain with her and the baby was his, and he did not want her made a public example.
“I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.” This is the prophecy the child of the Holy Ghost fulfils: seed out of David's bowels.
“The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.” Of the fruit of his body.
“That of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne.” The fruit of his loins: sperm. According to the flesh, not according to the spirit.
“Which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.” Made flesh and blood like you and I, like his brethren.

sense.text: The Lord told Ahaz, “Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God”, and Ahaz would not ask.

“Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel”, which means God with us. In that time Syria and Ephraim banded together to attack Judah, and as a sign that God would defend Judah this child would be born, symbolizing that God was with them.
“Before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings.” Before he learns right from wrong, both kings will be gone.

precepts.why:
“Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a man's pen concerning Maher–shalal–hash–baz”: quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil. As quick as they try to attack you, they will be destroyed.

“And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son.” Isaiah went in unto his wife and she conceived. “Then said the Lord to me, Call his name Maher–shalal–hash–baz.” The same way Gabriel named John and Christ before they were conceived, the Lord named Isaiah's son before he was conceived.

“For before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother, the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away”: the same as Isaiah 7:15. Assyria would come up, “And he shall pass through Judah”, reaching “even to the neck”, but not conquer it: “O Immanuel.” “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.” Once Isaiah's son was born, they could not conquer Judah.

“Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel.” Not his wife: Isaiah and the children are the signs. So the sign of Isaiah 7:14 was the child, not the virgin. The virgin birth is garbage.
“I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.” “Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity.” The man is the sign.
“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign: according to all that he hath done shall ye do.” Not his wife: Ezekiel. The Lord had him eat dung, and we ended up eating dung. “Thou shalt be a sign unto them.”

“There shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet. For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.” The men were always the signs. Hosea's marriage was a sign, but there is no scripture where a woman by herself is the sign.

Solomon says, “I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth”, Adam. “In my mother's womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood, of the seed of man.” “I was nursed in swaddling clothes”, and Christ was wrapped in swaddling clothes in Luke 2.

“For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth.” Is Christ our king? Was Solomon our king? Was David our king? Yes. “For all men have one entrance into life, and the like going out.” There is only one way all kings come into this world.

sense.text: Melchisedec, “King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem”: the king of peace, acknowledged as high priest by Abraham, who “gave a tenth part of all.”

“Without father, without mother, without descent.” This is no proof of a virgin birth. It speaks of a spiritual being in the heavens: no record of his lineage anywhere, no earthly father or mother, yet acknowledged as high priest by Abraham. Christ in the heavens had no earthly father or mother, but he had to be born into this world and become a son of man, made a little lower than the angels.

And the Christians cannot use it either: it says without father and without mother, and by their own doctrine Christ had a mother. This is a spiritual being, and Christ did not take on the nature of angels.
